title: Cartier to Hochelaga, with a winter at Stadacona, 1535–36
summary: With Taignoagny and Domagaya as guides, Cartier took three ships up the St Lawrence to Stadacona, and went on by pinnace to Hochelaga, a palisaded Iroquoian town under a mountain he named Mont Royal. He wintered at Stadacona; scurvy killed some twenty-five of his men until the Stadaconans gave them a cure. In May 1536 he took Donnacona and nine others to France by a trick.

events.label: Stadacona: Donnacona's town
events.text: Cartier and his ships were welcomed by Donnacona, who did not want him to go on to Hochelaga, a rival and trading town. Taignoagny and Domagaya were by then unwilling guides.

events.label: Hochelaga, and the mountain
events.text: A round town of some fifty houses, most of them longhouses, enclosed by a palisade three ranks deep. Cartier read the people the Gospel of John and the Passion, and named the mountain above the town Mont Royal. When he came back in 1541 he made no mention of the town, and where it stood is still not known.

events.label: Scurvy, and annedda
events.text: Some twenty-five of about a hundred and ten men died. Domagaya, who had been ill with it himself, showed the French a drink made from the bark and leaves of a tree called annedda, and the rest recovered. Which tree it was is not known; white cedar is the usual guess.

events.label: Donnacona and nine others taken
events.source: Donnacona (Wikipedia); Dictionary of Canadian Biography: seized at the feast of 3 May
events.text: Cartier invited Donnacona, Taignoagny, Domagaya and seven others to a feast at the fort, and sailed with them. He told the people Donnacona would be back within a year or so. The ten were presented at court; Donnacona died in France about 1539, and by 1541 all but a girl were dead.
